reference_prolog:
/*  Self-contained SWI-Prolog program (New Jersey, focus year 2021)

    Question: Must a landlord accept a tenant's attempt to cure for substantial damage to property?

    Statutes encoded (as provided):
      - NJ Rev Stat  2A:18-61.1 (2021)  (grounds; includes damage/injury to premises)
      - NJ Rev Stat  2A:18-61.2 (2021)  (notice periods; includes 3-day notice for injury)
      - NJ Rev Stat  2A:18-55 (2021)    (cure by paying rent in arrears into court; stops proceedings)
      - NJ Rev Stat  2A:42-10.16a (2021) (must accept rent payment within 3 business days after warrant/lockout for nonpayment)
*/

% -----------------------------
% Basic helpers / domain model
% -----------------------------

% We model eviction "reasons" as atoms.
eviction_reason(nonpayment_of_rent).
eviction_reason(injury_to_premises).          % substantial damage to property
eviction_reason(disorderly_conduct).
eviction_reason(habitual_failure_to_pay_rent).
eviction_reason(continued_violation_of_rules).
eviction_reason(substantial_breach_of_covenant).

% A "cure attempt" can be a rent payment cure or a repair cure.
cure_attempt_type(pay_rent_arrears).
cure_attempt_type(repair_damage).

% -----------------------------
% Statute translations
% -----------------------------

/*
  NJ Rev Stat  2A:18-61.1 (2021) - Grounds for removal, including:
    (a) fails to pay rent due and owing
    (c) willfully or by gross negligence caused/allowed destruction, damage, or injury to premises
*/
statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(nonpayment_of_rent) :- !.     % 2A:18-61.1(a)
statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(injury_to_premises) :- !.     % 2A:18-61.1(c)
statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(disorderly_conduct) :- !.     % 2A:18-61.1(b)
statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(habitual_failure_to_pay_rent) :- !. % 2A:18-61.1(j)
statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(continued_violation_of_rules) :- !. % 2A:18-61.1(d)
statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(substantial_breach_of_covenant) :- !. % 2A:18-61.1(e)

/*
  NJ Rev Stat  2A:18-61.2 (2021) - Notice required prior to institution of action.
  Key mapping from provided text:
    - For disorderly conduct (61.1(b)) or injury to premises (61.1(c)): 3 days' notice.
    - Exception: "No judgment ... except in the nonpayment of rent under subsection a. or f."
      (i.e., the statute's notice requirement does not apply to those nonpayment actions).
*/
statute_2a18_61_2_notice_days(injury_to_premises, 3) :- !.      % 2A:18-61.2(3)(a)
statute_2a18_61_2_notice_days(disorderly_conduct, 3) :- !.     % 2A:18-61.2(3)(a)
statute_2a18_61_2_notice_days(nonpayment_of_rent, 0) :- !.     % notice not required by 2A:18-61.2(3) exception

% For completeness (not needed to answer the question), include some additional mappings from 2A:18-61.2(3)(b).
statute_2a18_61_2_notice_days(continued_violation_of_rules, 30) :- !.     % one month's notice
statute_2a18_61_2_notice_days(substantial_breach_of_covenant, 30) :- !.
statute_2a18_61_2_notice_days(habitual_failure_to_pay_rent, 30) :- !.

/*
  NJ Rev Stat  2A:18-55 (2021) - Discontinuance upon payment into court of rent in arrears.
  Rule: In actions for nonpayment of rent (actions under 2A:18-53(b) as referenced),
  if tenant pays rent in default + accrued costs to clerk at any time on or before entry of final judgment,
  all proceedings shall be stopped.
*/
statute_2a18_55_cure_available_for_reason(nonpayment_of_rent) :- !.
statute_2a18_55_cure_available_for_reason(_OtherReason) :- fail.

statute_2a18_55_cure_stops_proceedings(Reason, PaymentTiming, PaymentMethod, IncludesCosts) :-
    statute_2a18_55_cure_available_for_reason(Reason),
    PaymentTiming = on_or_before_final_judgment,
    PaymentMethod = paid_to_court_clerk,
    IncludesCosts = includes_accrued_costs,
    !.

/*
  NJ Rev Stat  2A:42-10.16a (2021) - Three-day period for tenant to submit rent payment.
  Applies only to eviction actions for nonpayment of rent under 2A:18-61.1(a).
  Landlord shall accept payments made within three business days after warrant posted/lockout executed.
*/
statute_2a42_10_16a_cure_available_for_reason(nonpayment_of_rent) :- !.
statute_2a42_10_16a_cure_available_for_reason(_OtherReason) :- fail.

statute_2a42_10_16a_landlord_must_accept_payment(Reason, PaymentWindow) :-
    statute_2a42_10_16a_cure_available_for_reason(Reason),
    PaymentWindow = within_three_business_days_after_warrant_or_lockout,
    !.

% ------------------------------------
% Legal reasoning derived from statutes
% ------------------------------------

/* Determine whether any statute (in the provided set) imposes a duty to accept a "cure attempt"
   for a given eviction reason.

   In the provided statutes, "must accept" cure is explicit only for rent payment cures
   in nonpayment-of-rent cases (2A:42-10.16a). 2A:18-55 also provides a pay-into-court cure
   that stops proceedings, but is similarly limited to nonpayment actions.
*/
legal_landlord_must_accept_cure_attempt(EvictionReason, CureType, FactsTag) :-
    CureType = pay_rent_arrears,
    (   % Either cure path is sufficient to force acceptance/stop (as a practical duty),
        % but both are limited to nonpayment.
        FactsTag = facts_2a42_10_16a(PaymentWindow),
        statute_2a42_10_16a_landlord_must_accept_payment(EvictionReason, PaymentWindow)
    ;   FactsTag = facts_2a18_55(PaymentTiming, PaymentMethod, IncludesCosts),
        statute_2a18_55_cure_stops_proceedings(EvictionReason, PaymentTiming, PaymentMethod, IncludesCosts)
    ),
    !.
legal_landlord_must_accept_cure_attempt(_EvictionReason, _CureType, _FactsTag) :-
    fail.

% -----------------------------
% Scenario (facts from question)
% -----------------------------

% Jurisdiction / metadata
scenario_state(sc1, new_jersey).
scenario_focus_year(sc1, 2021).

% Core scenario: landlord is pursuing removal for substantial damage to property
scenario_residential_tenancy(sc1).
scenario_eviction_reason(sc1, injury_to_premises).

% Tenant attempts to "cure" substantial damage by repair (not by rent payment).
scenario_tenant_attempted_cure(sc1, repair_damage).

/* scenario_statement/0 succeeds when the encoded factual statement is satisfied.
   It intentionally mirrors the question's situation:
   - a residential NJ tenancy
   - eviction ground is substantial damage (injury to premises)
   - tenant attempts to cure by repairing the damage
*/
scenario_statement :-
    scenario_state(sc1, new_jersey),
    scenario_focus_year(sc1, 2021),
    scenario_residential_tenancy(sc1),
    scenario_eviction_reason(sc1, injury_to_premises),
    scenario_tenant_attempted_cure(sc1, repair_damage),
    statute_2a18_61_1_good_cause(injury_to_premises),
    !.

% Apply the legal rule to the scenario.
scenario_landlord_must_accept_cure(sc1) :-
    scenario_eviction_reason(sc1, Reason),
    scenario_tenant_attempted_cure(sc1, CureType),
    % The scenario has no rent-payment cure facts because it is a damage-to-premises case.
    legal_landlord_must_accept_cure_attempt(Reason, CureType, _AnyFactsTag),
    !.

scenario_landlord_must_accept_cure(_Scenario) :-
    fail.

% -----------------------------
% Answer
% -----------------------------

housing_answer(yes) :-
    scenario_statement,
    scenario_landlord_must_accept_cure(sc1),
    !.
housing_answer(no) :-
    scenario_statement,
    \+ scenario_landlord_must_accept_cure(sc1),
    !.

% -----------------------------
% Main entrypoint (required)
% -----------------------------

main :-
    housing_answer(Result),
    format('housing_answer(~w).~n', [Result]).


:- initialization(main, main).

expected.question: Must a landlord accept a tenant's attempt to cure for substantial damage to property?
